narrative:
The model predicts a 66% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This means the system sees a higher risk that you may not stay long-term with the organization.

Three factors stood out most in this decision. First, your total years of experience across all jobs had the strongest influence, pulling the prediction toward you staying. Most employees the model expects to remain have similar short experience levels of 1-5 years, so in this case your profile actually worked in your favor. 

However, two other factors pushed more strongly toward leaving. The fact that you have received other job opportunities while working here was the second most important driver, increasing the likelihood you might depart. Your employment in the "other" sector, which is less common among employees predicted to stay, also contributed to the higher risk of leaving.

The organization should consider discussing your external opportunities with you openly and exploring ways to strengthen your sense of long-term fit. You might reflect on whether additional responsibilities, clearer career growth, or improved alignment with your goals could increase your commitment. Addressing these areas could help reduce the risk the model has identified. (218 words)
